title: Mexico's Production: Taking a Hit Below the Border
section_path: Mexico's Production: Taking a Hit Below the Border
section_path_text: Mexico's Production: Taking a Hit Below the Border
summary:
Foreign investment
The steady decline of Mexico's crude oil production not only poses threats to the nation's GDP, but also to the health of the tanker market in the Caribbean basin. Mexican crude oil exports have fallen by a striking 1 million barrels per day (mbpd) since 2004 with total production rates now hovering around 2.5 million barrels per day. Now however, with support from President Enrique Pena Nieto, private investors may have the opportunity to reverse the country's crude oil fate.
